name: FoB Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Created by tournament in December 2003 and won by Jamie Noble over Kraven in the final. It changed hands four times inside six months and twice by vacancy — John Lennex gave it up on a call-up to Revenge, and Chaos won the five-way that replaced him — then stopped dead with Robbie Crockett's reign on 25 May 2004. The fed brought it back sixteen months later and put thirty-one men in a Rebirth match for it; Christopher Daniels won, and was still champion when the record ends.
notes: Transcribed complete from the fed's own published Championship Lineage (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-supercard-schedule-2005-09-29.html), which gives each reign's own length in days.

name: FoB Wrath Championship
epitaph: The Foundation of Brutality's second belt, crowned the same night as its first: Ozena beat Tony “The Marvel” Mason for it on 6 December 2003, then quit. Two of its four 2004 reigns started as vacancies and a third was simply handed to the number one contender, and it went dark with Tatewaki Kuno's on 25 May 2004 — the fed's own lineage lists it thereafter as a retired belt whose banner it no longer had. It was reinstated on 8 December 2005 with a division of its own, entered by beating a member of it, and Baxter Baxter beat Gene Snitsky to be its fifth champion.
notes: Transcribed complete from the fed's own published Championship Lineage (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-supercard-schedule-2005-09-29.html), which marks the belt “[Retired Belt, Banner Not Available.]”. The reinstated division's own rules are set out in the Sacrifice of 13 October 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-sacrifice-2005-10-13.html).

name: FoB Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held by exactly one team in its first life — Chris Harvard with Justin Credible, then with Shelton Benjamin after Credible left mid-reign — sixty-seven days that ran to 25 May 2004 and stopped. It came back with the promotion in September 2005 and moved three times in eighty-one days: The Butlers won a four-team tournament for it, the Detroit Street Thugs took it off them, and The Fear took it off the Thugs on 8 December 2005, the last change the lineage records.
notes: Transcribed complete from the fed's own published Championship Lineage (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-supercard-schedule-2005-09-29.html). The tournament final The Butlers won was a fatal four-way against the Marcello Family, the Sonic Death Monkeys and Alpha Gamma Sigma; none of the three is minted, their names standing in the served ledger itself.
